svg.title: An instruction is just wires
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch of a sixteen-bit Hack C-instruction drawn as sixteen labelled bit boxes with brackets peeling off each field to what it drives - the opcode, the a bit, the six ALU control pins, the three destination bits and the three jump bits - beside the fetch, decode, execute and write-back loop drawn around a central program counter, a hand-ruled trace table of a six-instruction program showing A, D, M and the PC after each step, a staircase pipeline diagram with one mispredicted branch crossed out in red, and a four-lane SIMD panel annotated with a measured 4.79 times speedup.
svg.text: ONE instruction: D = D + A is just 16 wires
a = use A, or the memory word M[A]
c1..c6 -> the six ALU control pins
d1 d2 d3 -> which of A, D, M is written
j1 j2 j3 -> compared against zr / ng
these ARE zx nx zy ny f no
the PC is the only state that decides what
a real trace: @2 / D=A / @3 / D=D+A / @0 / M=D
no magic left: A, D and M are registers; the PC just counts
branch mispredicted -> flush the pipe, ~15-20 cycles gone
the loop you wrote may not exist in the
